I keep replaying little things—him coming home late, a phone call he took in the hallway—and I’m convinced there was someone else, even though no one in the family agrees and there’s no real proof.

It’s not like I’m hearing voices or seeing things. It’s just this fixed idea that won’t budge. Most days I still get up, go to work, pay my bills, look after the flat. But every so often, maybe for a week or two at a time, I sink into this low mood—crying, not enjoying my soaps, feeling guilty that I wasn’t “good enough” for him. Then that passes, and I’m more or less back to my usual self, except the belief he cheated never goes away.

Sometimes, even at work washing dishes, I hear his voice, clear as day, arguing with her about keeping it secret from me, even though he’s been gone for years.

Most days I feel crushed, like there’s a heavy weight on my chest. I’m tired all the time, move slowly, and have to force myself to get to the kitchen. I don’t get any pleasure from anything anymore, just go through the motions. I feel worthless, stupid for not “seeing” it sooner, and I’ve had dark thoughts that maybe it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up.

There was a stretch, maybe a month, when the sadness eased a bit, but the certainty he’d cheated and the voices carried on just the same. Overall, though, the low mood and hopelessness have been there more often than not throughout these years.
